scale.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "amelyun [1 million]", "amelyar [1 billion]": each word has one fixed value.

group_mark.source: CLDR main/kab.xml, latn symbols: group U+00A0 (no-break space).

space_groups.source: CLDR main/kab.xml groups digits with a no-break space ("1 000 000").

plural_scale_needs_count.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "singular: alef ; plural: alaf": the plural follows a count ("telt-alaf").

scale_noun_agrees.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "The word for million is amelyun [1 million]", "The word for billion is amelyar [1 billion]"; the page gives no plural of either. In this lexicon both are numerals, which this setting does not reach.

joiner_tens_units.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "starting with the unit, followed by the conjunction u, then the ten (e.g.: setta u εecrin [26], tmanya u xemsin [58])".

joiner_after_hundred.source: No source shows how a hundred joins the rest of a number; the reader takes it with or without "u".

joiner_between_groups.source: No source shows how a thousand joins the rest of a number; the reader takes it with or without "u".

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No source shows "u" after alef; after "alef u" only a group below a hundred is read as well formed.

tens_order.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "starting with the unit, followed by the conjunction u, then the ten".

ordinal_style.source: en.wikipedia "Kabyle grammar", Numerotation, after Mettouchi et al. 2015 (CorpAfroAs), pp. 237-238: ordinals are wis (feminine tis) and the cardinal ("wis sin", "tis tlata"); "amezwaru" is first.

fold_marks.source: Kabyle Latin letters with a dot below or a caron (ḍ ṭ ẓ ṛ ḥ ṣ č ǧ) are often typed without the mark; the number words read the same.

letter_folds.source: apprendrelekabyle.com, "Les nombres en kabyle", writes "ṛebεa-mya" with Greek ε for ɛ; Greek ε and γ are common stand-ins for ɛ and ɣ.

joiner.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "How to count in Kabyle": "the conjunction u".

ordinal_particle.source: en.wiktionary, Module:number_list/data/kab and the entries "wis" (after Kossmann 2013): "forms ordinal numbers by preceding a cardinal number ... wis xemsa (fifth)", feminine tis; omniglot.com writes "wiss sin (m) tiss snat (f)".

decimal_marker.source: No source gives a word for the decimal mark.

minus.source: No source gives a word for minus.

range_cue.source: No source gives the Kabyle word for "between" before two numbers.

article_one.source: en.wikipedia "Kabyle grammar", Numerotation, after Mettouchi et al. 2015 (CorpAfroAs), pp. 237-238: yiwen (f. yiwet) "one" also marks a noun indefinite ("yiwen wergaz").

minus_idioms.source: No source gives such a word in a Kabyle number.
